validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification/duplicate/location — real, FERC-certificated interstate transmission pipeline, correctly classified, not a duplicate of any other roster row
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE confirmed beyond doubt: NEXUS Gas Transmission, LLC is the applicant of record in FERC Docket No. CP16-22-000; the Commission's own certificate order (NEXUS Gas Transmission, LLC, 160 FERC P 61,022, issued 2017-08-25, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-08/CP16-22.pdf) authorizes construction and operation. Independent, non-GEM corroboration that this is a real, currently-operating asset (not GEM-only/hallucinated): a 2020 FERC Federal Register notice (85 FR 40640, Docket CP16-22-000, 2020-07-07) confirms NEXUS 'commenced service on the majority of the NEXUS Project on October 13, 2018'; Enbridge's own current (dated 2026) corporate Energy Infrastructure Assets factsheet lists it as an operating asset; DT Midstream's own current asset page (dtmidstream.com/asset/nexus-gas-transmission-pipeline/, dateModified 2026-03-26) lists it as 'Operational'; contemporaneous AP/Detroit News (2017-08-27, via Wayback) and Canton Rep (2017-12-26, via Wayback) newspaper coverage describe the same physical project under construction; and Enbridge's own Nov 2018 corporate announcement (via Wayback) describes it having 'recently entered service.' CLASSIFICATION correct: this is a FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission trunk line (36-inch mainline, four new compressor stations), not a gathering/feeder system — confirmed by the FERC order's own facilities description and by every independent source read. Fuel=Gas trivially confirmed by all sources. DUPLICATE check against the full 46-row Appalachian roster: no other row describes this project or route. The roster's two 'Vector Gas Pipeline'-named rows (P2505 'Blue Water Energy Center (BWEC) Pipeline', P3202 'Blue Water Compressor Project') are 2021/2022-vintage Michigan/Wisconsin segments tied to a gas-fired power plant, physically and temporally distinct from the much older Vector Pipeline lease segments (Milford Segment, Belle River Segment, in service since the 1999-era historic Vector Pipeline system) that the NEXUS FERC order describes NEXUS leasing capacity from — see cross_row_leads for a possible roster-coverage gap this surfaces, not a duplicate of THIS row. LOCATION StartLocation='Kensington'/StartState='Ohio' and EndLocation='Willow Run'/EndState='Michigan' are BOTH precisely confirmed by the FERC order's own text: the mainline 'originat[es] at the existing Kensington Processing Plant in Hanover Township, Columbiana County, Ohio' and connects via 'a new interconnect (Willow Run) between NEXUS and DTE Gas in Ypsilanti Township, [Washtenaw County,] Michigan' (FERC order paras. 3, 7) — not a state-column defect. FUELSOURCE 'Marcellus and Utica shale fields' independently confirmed by DT Midstream's current page ('natural gas from the Marcellus/Utica shale formations in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia') and by Enbridge's own 2013 SEC Form 6-K describing the original 2012 proposal to move 'Ohio Utica shale gas.' CAVEAT (folded in here rather than a separate concern since it does not change any recommended value): the Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Ongoing Projects' PDF (Oct. 2018 issue) lists NEXUS's Diameter as '42 inches' — this is a genuine trade-press outlier, contradicted by BOTH the primary FERC certificate order (which states 'approximately 209.8 miles of new 36-inch-diameter pipeline' in Ohio plus 'approximately 46.8 miles of new 36-inch-diameter pipeline' in Michigan — no 42-inch segment anywhere in the facilities description) and by Enbridge's own current factsheet ('NEXUS is a 36-inch, 257-mile interstate pipeline'). GEM's current Diameter=36in is correct; the PGJ '42 inches' entry is not adopted. Length is likewise well-corroborated within normal rounding (FERC's own two segments sum to 256.6 mi; Canton Rep and PGJ both say 255 mi; Enbridge's factsheet says 257 mi; DT Midstream and Enbridge's Nov 2018 story both say 256 mi) — GEM's 255 mi sits squarely inside this tight, multiply-corroborated cluster, no correction needed. Opened and read to exhaustion all 10 harvested wiki citations plus several additional primary sources found via the FERC/SEC/Federal-Register source ladder; 2 of the 10 harvested citations were dead/unusable and are not cited anywhere in this shard: dtemidstream.com/location/nexus-pipeline/ (the domain has been squatted and now serves an unrelated Indonesian-language online-gambling page — genuinely dead content, no Wayback snapshot exists either, CDX API returns an empty snapshot set) and fractracker.org/2020/02/national-energy-petrochemical-map/ (a genuine 200 page but a generic multi-project map article that never names NEXUS — not a ref for this specific pipeline). eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php and the facebook.com/MedinaNOnexus citation were also opened and rejected: the former is a generic data-portal landing page with zero NEXUS-specific content, the latter now 404s.

validity.recommendation: update Owner1 (or Owner2, whichever slot currently reads 'DTE Energy') from 'DTE Energy' to 'DT Midstream' to reflect current corporate structure; DTE Energy spun off its midstream/pipeline business as the separately-traded company DT Midstream, Inc. in 2021, and DT Midstream (not DTE Energy) has held the 50% non-Enbridge NEXUS interest ever since
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's current Owner1/Owner2 values (DTE Energy 50%, Enbridge 50%) were CORRECT AT THE TIME NEXUS was certificated and entered service: FERC's 2017 order (para. 6, CP16-22-000) states NEXUS 'is jointly owned by indirect, wholly-owned subsidiaries of Spectra Energy Partners, LP (Spectra Energy, 50 percent) and DTE Energy Company (DTE Energy, 50 percent),' with footnote 4 noting 'On February 27, 2017, Spectra Energy became an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of Enbridge Inc.' — i.e., 'Enbridge' is the correct successor name for the Spectra Energy 50% slot, which GEM already has right. Contemporaneous press (Detroit News 2017-08-27: 'a partnership between Calgary, Alberta-based Enbridge and Detroit-based DTE Energy'; Canton Rep 2017-12-26: 'Detroit-based DTE Energy and Enbridge ... are partners') independently confirms this was the accurate ownership description in 2017. However, this is now STALE: DTE Energy spun off its non-utility midstream/pipeline assets (including its NEXUS interest) as DT Midstream, Inc., an independently publicly-traded company, in 2021. DT Midstream's OWN current asset page (dtmidstream.com/asset/nexus-gas-transmission-pipeline/, first published 2021-05-07, last modified 2026-03-26 — i.e. current as of this research) lists NEXUS Gas Transmission Pipeline among ITS OWN assets and states explicitly: 'It is a joint venture between Enbridge Inc. (50%) and DT Midstream (50%), and is operated by Enbridge Inc.' Enbridge's own current factsheet corroborates the 50/50 Enbridge/DT Midstream framing ('NEXUS is a 50/50 joint venture between Enbridge and DT Midstream'). Both current co-owners' own primary corporate materials — two independent origins — now name 'DT Midstream,' not 'DTE Energy,' as the non-Enbridge 50% owner. Recommend the sheet be updated to 'DT Midstream' for the current owner value (retaining 'DTE Energy' only if the sheet intends to preserve a historical/at-certification ownership snapshot, in which case a note distinguishing current vs. as-certificated ownership would resolve the ambiguity).

validity.recommendation: flag Capacity=1500 MMcf/d as the FERC-certificated/historical design figure; both current co-owners' own asset pages now state ~1.4 Bcf/d as the current design capacity — a genuine ~7% discrepancy worth a researcher note or a distinct current-vs-certificated capacity field, not a silent overwrite in either direction
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=1500 MMcf/d is well-corroborated as the ORIGINAL FERC-CERTIFICATED figure: the FERC order itself, the 2020 Federal Register notice ('the total 1,500,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of certificated capacity' — Dth/d and MMcf/d are treated as numerically equivalent in this docket), the Pipeline & Gas Journal Oct-2018 Ongoing Projects PDF ('Capacity: 1.5 Bcf/d'), and contemporaneous 2017 press (Detroit News: 'capable of carrying 1.5 billion cubic f[eet]'; Canton Rep: 'will carry up to 1.5 billion cubic feet') all independently agree on 1.5 Bcf/d = 1500 MMcf/d as the certificated/design capacity at construction. HOWEVER, both current co-owners' own current-day asset pages give a materially lower figure: DT Midstream's page states the system has 'current capacity of approximately 1.4 Bcf per day,' and Enbridge's own current factsheet states 'Design capacity: Up to 1.4 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d).' This is not a single-source outlier — it is the SAME lower figure independently restated by both 50/50 joint-venture partners on their own most-current asset pages, a materially different (~7%, ~100 MMcf/d) number from the certificated 1500 figure, and it postdates the certificate by several years. Plausible explanations (not resolved with material in hand): the certificated 1,500,000 Dth/d volume was never fully subscribed/utilized at 100% of nameplate (the 2020 Federal Register notice itself notes NEXUS had only 'increased firm commitments ... to more than 1,315,000 Dth/d' as of mid-2020, short of the full 1.5 Bcf/d), or the owners' marketing copy is describing subscribed/contracted-plus-headroom capacity rather than engineered/certificated capacity, or a physical derate. Recommend keeping 1500 as the certificated/historical value with a note, OR adding a distinct 'current design capacity ~1.4 Bcf/d per current owner disclosures' annotation — flagging for a researcher/Baird decision rather than silently picking one number.

cross_row_leads.facts: The NEXUS FERC order describes NEXUS leasing existing firm capacity from 'Vector Pipeline, L.P.' (docket CP16-102-000/CP16-4-000) via two specific segments: the 'Milford Segment' (interconnect between DTE Gas and Vector near Milford, Michigan) and the 'Belle River Segment' (interconnect near Belle River, Michigan), for 455,000 Dth/d, under a 15-year Capacity Lease Agreement. These are OLDER, pre-existing Vector Pipeline trunk segments (Vector in service since 1999-2000, a JV between Enbridge and DTE Energy) — physically and temporally distinct from this roster's two 'Vector Gas Pipeline'-named rows, P2505 ('Blue Water Energy Center (BWEC) Pipeline', StartYear1=2021) and P3202 ('Blue Water Compressor Project', StartYear1=2022), which are much newer segments tied to a Michigan gas-fired power plant. Flagging as a possible roster-coverage question: the historic Vector Pipeline trunk itself (the entity actually leasing capacity to NEXUS at Milford/Belle River) does not appear to be represented by either P2505 or P3202 under its own right — worth checking whether GEM tracks the main Vector Pipeline system anywhere, or only these two later lateral/compressor additions.

Same Vector Pipeline Milford/Belle River lease-segment observation as the P2505 lead above — flagging both of the roster's 'Vector'-named rows since it is not obvious from the FERC order alone which (if either) row's underlying corridor overlaps the leased segments; a researcher with access to Vector's own route map should confirm whether P2505/P3202 are unrelated additions (as their 2021/2022 start years suggest) or share physical pipe with the older Milford/Belle River segments.

summary: P0225 confirmed real, correctly classified (FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission), correctly located, and not a duplicate of any other roster row (including the two similarly-named 'Vector Gas Pipeline' rows, which are unrelated newer segments).
